docs.title: Documentation layers
docs.text: The MiaCaoMigo Engineering portal separates documentation by purpose, not by file format. Use this page to decide where new content belongs and to avoid duplicating the same topic in multiple places.

docs.title: Layer map
docs.text: Layer Directory Audience Typical content Planning 01_Planning/ Team, demos, onboarding Sprints, user stories, operational scenarios, ecosystem narrative Requirements 02_Requirements/ Engineering, evaluation RF, RNF, business rules, acceptance criteria, implementation matrix Diagrams 03_Diagrams/ Analysts, DB engineers ER models, attribute semantics (conceptual) Architecture 04_Architecture/ Developers, defense System view, application flows, database governance and schemas Academic deliverables 05_Docs/ Teachers, defense Official statements, academic reports, presentation guides Performance 06_Performance/ APS / quality evidence Strategy, measurements, recommendations Production 07_Deployment/ Teachers, defense, deployment operators Docker production mode, startup steps, environment variables, operational checklist

docs.title: Planning vs requirements
docs.text:
• Planning answers who does what in the clinic story (personas, timelines, OPS scenarios).
  • Requirements answers what the system must do (RF, RN, AC) and how far it is implemented.

Do not copy full RF tables into planning files. Link to 02_Requirements/ instead.

docs.title: Diagrams vs database architecture
docs.text:
Question Use Why does this entity exist? What does an attribute mean? 03_Diagrams/00_ER_Model/ER_V10/Atributos/ How is it implemented in PostgreSQL? 04_Architecture/01_Database/01_Schemas/ and SchemaSpy output Interactive table/column browser 04_Architecture/01_Database/03_SchemaSpy/02_Output/

These views are complementary, not duplicates.

docs.title: Application architecture vs academic report
docs.text:
Type Location Technical flows, API, runtime, implementation evidence 04_Architecture/02_Application/ Defense-oriented narrative, 15 min presentation, screenshots checklist 05_Docs/01_Academic_Reports/ and 05_Docs/02_Presentation/

The application report under 05_Docs is the canonical academic document; architecture pages link to it.

docs.title: Academic vs production
docs.text:
Type Location Defense narrative, reports and presentation support 05_Docs/ Practical production startup guide and Docker deployment steps 07_Deployment/

The production guide is written for academic demonstration first: it explains how the system would be started in a production-like Docker setup without requiring a full public cloud deployment.

It also documents what is already production-aligned (Docker prod compose, isolated DB, secrets via env, static docs, healthchecks) and what would still be needed in industry (HTTPS, reverse proxy, CI/CD, automated backups, centralized monitoring). See Production guide.

docs.title: Instruções para testar o projeto MiaCaoMigo
docs.text:
Suadações, Professora,

Para testar o projeto é necessário clonar os 3 repositórios e arrancar os serviços por esta ordem:

  1. DataLayer
  2. Website / API
  3. Engineering Docs

docs.title: Repositórios
docs.text:
Application / Website:

https://github.com/JMRM98/MiaCaoMigo_.git

DataLayer / Base de Dados:

https://github.com/bulletproof20/MiaCaoMigo_DataLayer.git

Engineering / Documentação:

https://github.com/bulletproof20/MiaCaoMigo_Engineering.git

docs.title: Pré-requisitos
docs.text:
• Docker + Docker Compose
  • Node.js + npm
  • Portas livres:
  • 5433 para PostgreSQL
  • 3000 para o website/API
  • 8000 para a documentação Engineering

docs.title: 1. Clonar os repositórios
docs.text:
mkdir MiaCaoMigo
cd MiaCaoMigo

git clone https://github.com/bulletproof20/MiaCaoMigo_DataLayer.git
git clone https://github.com/JMRM98/MiaCaoMigo_.git
git clone https://github.com/bulletproof20/MiaCaoMigo_Engineering.git

docs.title: 2. Arrancar a base de dados
docs.text:
cd MiaCaoMigo_DataLayer
docker compose up -d --build

A base de dados fica disponível em:

Host: localhost
Porta: 5433
Database: miacaomigo
User: postgres
Password: 1234

docs.title: 3. Arrancar o website/API
docs.text:
cd ../MiaCaoMigo_
npm install
npm start

Se o ficheiro Backend/.env não existir, criar com:

DB_USER=postgres
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_NAME=miacaomigo
DB_PASSWORD=1234
DB_PORT=5433

JWT_SECRET=EsteSegredo!2026!ProgWeb
JWT_EXPIRES_IN=6h

PORT=3000
API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000

Depois abrir:

Website: http://localhost:3000
Swagger/API Docs: http://localhost:3000/api-docs/
OpenAPI JSON: http://localhost:3000/api-docs.json

docs.title: 4. Arrancar a documentação Engineering
docs.text:
Noutro terminal:

cd MiaCaoMigo_Engineering
docker compose -f .docs/docker-compose.yml up -d

Abrir:

Documentação Engineering: http://localhost:8000

docs.title: Sugestão de teste rápido
docs.text:
1. Entrar no website em http://localhost:3000.
  2. Fazer login como cliente.
  3. Validar a área do cliente:
  4. consultas;
  5. prescrições;
  6. faturas;
  7. download de PDFs.
  8. Fazer logout.
  9. Fazer login como staff/admin com 2@miacaomigo.pt.
  10. Validar:
  11. área comercial;
  12. histórico/detalhes de faturas;
  13. download de PDF de fatura;
  14. gestão de consultas;
  15. marcação/reagendamento de consultas.
  16. Abrir Swagger em http://localhost:3000/api-docs/ para consultar/testar endpoints.
  17. Abrir a documentação Engineering em http://localhost:8000.

docs.title: Nota sobre PDFs
docs.text:
Os PDFs de faturas e prescrições são gerados no momento do clique em "PDF".

Os ficheiros não ficam guardados na base de dados como binários; o backend gera o documento em memória e envia-o ao browser, são descarregados os ficheiros para o computador do utilizador.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: MiaCaoMigo Engineering   Central Engineering & Architecture Portal    Central documentation platform dedicated to the planning, modeling, architecture and technical documentation of the MiaCaoMigo ecosystem.  This portal aggregates conceptual, operational and engineering documentation produced throughout the academic project lifecycle.

docs.title: About the documentation
docs.text:
This platform centralizes the different documentation layers developed during the MiaCaoMigo project, including:

  • project planning and sprint evolution;
  • functional and non-functional requirements;
  • operational and ecosystem narratives;
  • conceptual and structural modeling;
  • system and database architecture;
  • governance and engineering standards;
  • technical and academic deliverables.

The documentation is organized progressively, allowing both high-level conceptual understanding and deeper technical exploration.

Layer model: DOCUMENTATION_LAYERS.md — what belongs in Planning, Diagrams, Architecture, and User Stories.

docs.title: Sprint 3 — Cenários de Uso, User Stories e Diagrama de Estados
Objetivo da Sprint
docs.text:
Esta sprint foca a evolução do sistema MiaCaoMigo para a clínica veterinária, privilegiando a integração entre o website e a base de dados. As entregas centrais são:

  • Seleção de CdU prioritários.
  • Narrativas de fluxo principal e fluxos alternativos.
  • User Stories com critérios de aceitação.
  • Mockups de interface para os requisitos selecionados.
  • Diagrama de estados para uma classe mais adequada.

docs.title: CdU Prioritários Selecionados
docs.text:
Escolhemos dois CdU principais que são críticos para o funcionamento da clínica e têm impacto direto na aplicação web e na base de dados:

  1. Autenticar Usuário
  2. Permite que clientes e funcionários façam login no sistema.

  3. É pré-requisito para consultar e agendar consultas.

  4. Agendar Consulta

  5. Permite que um cliente marque uma consulta para o seu animal.
  6. Inclui também a visão de consulta por functionário e a mudança de estado da consulta.

docs.title: Cliente — Mariana
docs.text:
• Tem 28 anos e é dona de um cão e um gato.
  • Usa o site para marcar consultas, ver histórico e consultar status das consultas.
  • Precisa de um processo rápido e claro, com confirmação visível após marcar.

docs.title: Funcionário/Veterinário — Dr. João
docs.text:
• Utiliza o sistema para iniciar e fechar consultas.
  • Consulta marcações dos clientes e gere horários.
  • Precisa de informações imediatas do cliente e do animal.

docs.title: Descrição
docs.text: O sistema permite que um utilizador existente faça login com e-mail e password. O login carrega um JWT que identifica se o utilizador é cliente ou staff.

docs.title: Fluxo Principal
docs.text:
1. O utilizador abre a página de login.
  2. O utilizador insere o e-mail e a password.
  3. O sistema valida as credenciais.
  4. Se as credenciais estiverem corretas, o sistema emite um token JWT.
  5. O utilizador recebe confirmação de login e é redirecionado para a página inicial ou painel.

docs.title: Fluxos Alternativos
docs.text:
• A1: E-mail não encontrado.
  • O sistema mostra a mensagem "Conta não encontrada."

  • O utilizador permanece na página de login.

  • A2: Password incorreta.

  • O sistema mostra a mensagem "Password incorreta."

  • O utilizador pode tentar novamente.

  • A3: Conta desativada.

  • O sistema mostra a mensagem "Conta desativada. Contacte a clínica."

  • A4: Já existe sessão ativa.

  • O sistema mostra a mensagem "Já existe uma sessão ativa."

docs.title: US1 - Login do Cliente
docs.text:
Como cliente, quero autenticar-me com e-mail e password, para aceder ao meu histórico de consultas e marcar novas consultas.

Critérios de aceitação:

  • O formulário aceita e-mail e password.
  • O sistema valida entrada não vazia.
  • Em caso de sucesso, retorna token JWT e dados do utilizador.
  • Em caso de falha, mostra mensagem de erro adequada.

docs.title: US2 - Login do Funcionário
docs.text:
Como funcionário, quero entrar no sistema com o meu e-mail institucional, para poder aceder às funções de gestão de consultas.

Critérios de aceitação:

  • O login valida e-mail e password.
  • Identifica se o utilizador é staff a partir do e-mail.
  • Se staff, retorna a lista de permissões.

docs.title: TC1 - Login com sucesso (cliente)
docs.text:
• Dado que o cliente tem conta válida,
  • Quando inserir e-mail e password corretos,
  • Então o sistema deve retornar token JWT e success: true.

docs.title: TC2 - Login com e-mail inválido
docs.text:
• Dado que o e-mail não existe,
  • Quando tentar autenticar,
  • Então o sistema deve retornar status 401 e mensagem "Conta não encontrada.".

docs.title: TC3 - Login com password errada
docs.text:
• Dado que o e-mail existe e a password está errada,
  • Quando submeter o formulário,
  • Então o sistema deve retornar status 401 e mensagem "Password incorreta.".

docs.title: Descrição
docs.text: O sistema permite que um cliente marque uma nova consulta para o seu animal e que um funcionário visualize todas as consultas e atualize o estado de uma consulta.

docs.title: Fluxo Principal
docs.text:
1. O cliente autenticado acede ao painel de marcação de consultas.
  2. Seleciona o animal e a data/hora desejada.
  3. Escolhe um veterinário disponível.
  4. Submete o pedido de marcação.
  5. O sistema grava a consulta na tabela appointment.
  6. O cliente recebe confirmação de que a consulta foi criada.

docs.title: Fluxos Alternativos
docs.text:
• A1: Campos obrigatórios em falta.
  • O sistema sinaliza os campos que faltam.

  • O cliente corrige e tenta novamente.

  • A2: Veterinário indisponível / erro de FK.

  • O sistema devolve erro se id_vet ou id_usr não existir.

  • O cliente/funcionário escolhe outro veterinário ou verifica os dados.

  • A3: Staff cria consulta em nome de cliente.

  • Um funcionário preenche id_usr do cliente.

  • O sistema valida se o cliente existe e cria a consulta.

  • A4: Cliente tenta ver consultas de outro cliente.

  • O sistema devolve 403 e nega o acesso.

docs.title: US3 - Marcar Consulta como Cliente
docs.text:
Como cliente autenticado, quero agendar uma consulta para o meu animal, para receber atendimento veterinário.

Critérios de aceitação:

  • O cliente só consegue marcar consultas quando autenticado.
  • O formulário pede animal, data/hora e veterinário.
  • A API grava o registo na tabela appointment.
  • O cliente vê confirmação de sucesso.

docs.title: US4 - Ver histórico de consultas do cliente
docs.text:
Como cliente, quero ver a lista das minhas consultas marcadas, para saber quando ocorrerão e o seu estado.

Critérios de aceitação:

  • O cliente só vê as próprias consultas.
  • O sistema usa /appointments/client/:id_usr.
  • Consultas de outros clientes não são visíveis.

docs.title: US5 - Iniciar e Encerrar Consulta (staff)
docs.text:
Como funcionário, quero iniciar e fechar uma consulta, para registar quando a consulta começou e terminou.

Critérios de aceitação:

  • Staff autorizado acede às rotas PATCH /appointments/:id_app/start e /appointments/:id_app/close.
  • O estado temporal da consulta é atualizado no banco.
  • Se a consulta não existir, o sistema devolve 404.

docs.title: TC4 - Marcar consulta com sucesso
docs.text:
• Dado um cliente autenticado com animal cadastrado,
  • Quando submeter data, veterinário e animal válidos,
  • Então a API deve retornar status 201 e o registo appointment criado.

docs.title: TC5 - Visualizar próprias consultas
docs.text:
• Dado um cliente autenticado,
  • Quando aceder à rota /appointments/client/:id_usr com o seu id,
  • Então o sistema retorna apenas as consultas desse cliente.

docs.title: TC6 - Iniciar consulta como staff
docs.text:
• Dado um staff autenticado,
  • Quando submeter PATCH /appointments/:id_app/start para uma consulta existente,
  • Então o registo deve ter sta_dat_app preenchido.

docs.title: TC7 - Encerrar consulta como staff
docs.text:
• Dado um staff autenticado,
  • Quando submeter PATCH /appointments/:id_app/close para uma consulta existente,
  • Então o registo deve ter end_dat_app preenchido.

docs.title: Mockup 1 — Página de Login
docs.text:
Elementos principais:

  • Campo E-mail
  • Campo Password
  • Botão Entrar
  • Espaço para mensagens de erro
  • Link de recuperação de password (opcional)

O layout deve ser simples e responsivo, com entrada centralizada e feedback claro.

docs.title: Mockup 2 — Página de Agendamento de Consulta
docs.text:
Elementos principais:

  • Dropdown Animal
  • Campo Data e Hora
  • Dropdown Veterinário
  • Botão Confirmar consulta
  • Resumo da consulta após submissão
  • Mensagens de validação em linha

O cliente deve perceber facilmente quais são os campos obrigatórios.

docs.title: Mockup 3 — Painel de Consultas do Cliente
docs.text:
Elementos principais:

  • Lista de consultas agendadas
  • Estado da consulta (Agendada, Em Curso, Concluída)
  • Data/hora, veterinário e animal
  • Link para detalhes da consulta

Deve permitir confirmar que a consulta está registada e visualizar o histórico.

docs.title: Diagrama de Estados — Classe Appointment
docs.text:
A classe mais adequada para o diagrama de estados é Appointment, pois o fluxo de vida da consulta implica transições de estado explícitas.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Scheduled
    Scheduled --> InProgress: iniciar consulta
    InProgress --> Completed: encerrar consulta
    Scheduled --> Cancelled: cancelar consulta
    InProgress --> Cancelled: cancelar em curso
    Completed --> [*]
    Cancelled --> [*]

    state Scheduled {
      [*] --> AwaitingConfirmation
      AwaitingConfirmation --> Confirmed: confirmar agendamento
    }

docs.title: Observações
docs.text:
• O sistema atual já implementa a criação e as transições start / close.
  • A transição cancel pode ser adicionada em sprints futuras.

docs.title: Como Usar este Documento
docs.text:
1. Rever os CdU com a equipa e validar se estes são os de maior prioridade na sprint.
  2. Implementar primeiro a autenticação e depois o agendamento de consultas.
  3. Usar os mockups como guia para o desenvolvimento frontend.
  4. Validar cada US com os testes de aceitação propostos.

docs.title: Referências Técnicas
docs.text:
• API de agendamento: POST /appointments, GET /appointments/client/:id_usr, PATCH /appointments/:id_app/start, PATCH /appointments/:id_app/close
  • API de autenticação: POST /users/auth/login, GET /users/auth/me
  • Tabelas relevantes na base de dados: user_account, login_record, appointment, animal, employee, client.

docs.title: Sprint 4 — Modulo 2: Gestao de Animais
docs.text:
Analise de rastreabilidade entre a especificacao da Sprint 4 e a implementacao real do Modulo 2, focada em Gestao de Animais.

Fonte funcional analisada: Sprint 04.pdf (assumindo que o PDF contém os requisitos para este módulo).

Repositorios verificados:

  • Aplicacao/API: MiaCaoMigo_
  • Base de dados/QA: MiaCaoMigo_DataLayer

Legenda:

  • Implementado: existe fluxo funcional e/ou regra executavel no frontend, API ou base de dados.
  • Parcial: existe parte relevante, mas falta um detalhe pedido no PDF.
  • Nao evidenciado: nao foi encontrada implementacao real suficiente.

docs.title: Sumario Executivo
docs.text:
O Módulo 2 está implementado para os fluxos principais de registo de animais, gestão de posse (associação cliente-animal), listagem de espécies e raças, listagem de animais para adoção e o processo de adoção por parte do cliente. A camada de base de dados inclui validações robustas para a consistência da posse e dados do animal.

As principais lacunas face a um sistema completo de gestão de animais (e inferidas do contexto disponível) são:

  • Gestão de Ciclo de Vida do Animal: Embora existam estados como 'Falecido' e 'Adotado' na lógica de negócio da base de dados, a interface/API para gerir explicitamente o ciclo de vida completo do animal (e.g., desativar, marcar como falecido) não foi evidenciada.
  • Gestão de Entregas/Resgates: As funções de base de dados suportam a consistência temporal de datas de entrega e resgate, mas não foram encontrados endpoints de API ou interfaces de utilizador para registar e gerir estes processos.
  • Histórico de Posse: A base de dados impede posses sobrepostas, mas não há um fluxo claro na API/UI para consultar o histórico completo de posse de um animal.
  • Gestão de Fotos: O modelo de dados prevê um photo_path para animais de adoção, mas não há endpoints de API para upload ou gestão de fotos.

Fonte funcional analisada: Sprint 04.pdf.

Repositorios verificados:

  • Aplicacao/API: MiaCaoMigo_
  • Base de dados/QA: MiaCaoMigo_DataLayer

Legenda:

  • Implementado: existe fluxo funcional e/ou regra executavel no frontend, API ou base de dados.

docs.title: Sumario Executivo
docs.text:
O Modulo 3 esta implementado para os fluxos principais de catalogo, consulta de stock, reposicao por compra, venda ao balcao, emissao/listagem/download de faturas, devolucoes e atualizacao automatica de stock.

As principais lacunas face ao PDF sao:

  • RF_M3_01: existe criacao e consulta de produtos, mas nao foi encontrada edicao/desativacao via API/UI.
  • RF_M3_05 / RF_M3_06: existe registo de compras/reposicao, mas nao ha fornecedor formal associado no fluxo aplicacional.
  • RF_M3_08 / RF_M3_21 / RF_M3_22 / RF_M3_23: metodo de pagamento e estados existem no modelo, mas nao ha fluxo completo de pagamentos; vendas ao balcao criam fatura diretamente como paid.
  • RF_M3_16: a selecao de lote e automatica/FIFO na base de dados; nao ha selecao manual pelo utilizador.
  • RF_M3_18: a ligacao fatura-consulta existe estruturalmente, mas nao foi encontrada geracao/associacao automaticas a partir do fecho de consulta.
  • RF_M3_29 / RF_M3_30: existem vistas de stock e historicos operacionais, mas nao ha relatorios analiticos completos de vendas/faturacao/produtos mais usados.

docs.title: Notas de Cobertura Tecnica
docs.text:
• sp_receive_purchase nao impede segunda rececao de uma compra ja received, podendo duplicar stock; nao foi encontrado teste de integridade para este procedimento.
  • Ao receber compra, sp_receive_purchase grava val_dat_sto = null em stock, pelo que a validade recolhida em purchase_line nao e propagada automaticamente.
  • Nao existe entidade payment nem estado partial em invoice_status; sta_inv nao e atualizado por soma de pagamentos (apenas por DML/demo ou criacao direta como paid na app).
  • Nao existe DataBase/QA/05_Manual/03_Module3/ (Mod1 e Mod4 tem scripts de defesa manual).
  • Consumo clinico no Mod4 (tfn_deduct_product_stock em rel_app_product) nao segue o FIFO de tfn_stock_after_sale — dois caminhos de reducao de stock coexistem.
  • DataBase/Schema/03_Module3_Commercial_Management/06_Jobs_Mod3.sql e placeholder (sem jobs agendados).
  • DataBase/Queries/03_Module3/queries_03Module.sql esta marcado como deprecado e referencia colunas inexistentes (stock_minimo em vez de min_sto).

docs.title: Sprint 4 — Modulo 4: Consultas / Appointments
docs.text:
Analise de rastreabilidade entre a especificacao da Sprint 4 e a implementacao real do Modulo 4, focada em Gestao Clinica / Consultas.

Fonte funcional analisada: Sprint 04.pdf.

Repositorios verificados:

  • Aplicacao/API: MiaCaoMigo_
  • Base de dados/QA: MiaCaoMigo_DataLayer

Legenda:

  • Implementado: existe fluxo funcional e/ou regra executavel no frontend, API ou base de dados.
  • Parcial: existe parte relevante, mas falta um detalhe pedido no PDF.
  • Nao evidenciado: nao foi encontrada implementacao real suficiente.

docs.title: Sumario Executivo
docs.text:
O Modulo 4 esta implementado para o ciclo principal de consultas: marcacao, listagem, disponibilidade por veterinario, validacao de animal/cliente/veterinario/especialidade, cancelamento, reagendamento, inicio, sala de espera, conclusao, registo clinico, historico, prescricoes simples, PDF de prescricao, produtos usados em consulta e notificacoes.

As principais lacunas face ao PDF sao:

  • RF_M4_07 / RN_M4_07: a conclusao da consulta nao exige diagnostico obrigatorio. O backend aceita dia_app nulo ao fechar a consulta.
  • RF_M4_08 / RN_M4_09: a prescricao existe, mas nao tem campo de validade nem regra de validade maxima de 30 dias.
  • RF_M4_15: existe estado no_show e job automatico, mas nao ha acao manual de staff para marcar uma consulta como nao realizada no fluxo web.
  • RF_M4_17 / RN_M4_16 / RN_M4_17: existe ligacao tecnica consulta-fatura, mas nao foi encontrada geracao automatica de fatura ao concluir consulta.

docs.title: Narrative Stories — MiaCaoMigo Braga (May–June 2026)
docs.text: Human-readable narratives drawn from the same launch simulation as 02_Operational_Scenarios. Master context: 00_ECOSYSTEM.md · Chronology: TIMELINE_LAUNCH_2026.md.

docs.title: Purpose of this layer
docs.text:
The operational folder documents who did what, when, and under which rules — appointment states, commercial events, absence codes, and cross-links for DemoData and QA. That material is precise and schematic by design.

Narrative Stories translate those facts into coherent, readable accounts of people, animals, and partner organisations. The goal is ecosystem understanding: roles, relationships, and the rhythm of the first operational weeks — not implementation detail.

Layer Audience question Where Narrative Stories (here) Who are they, and how do their paths intersect? 01_Narrative_Stories/ Operational Scenarios What exactly happened, and what must the system enforce? 02_Operational_Scenarios/

Operational validation, state names, and chronological indexes remain authoritative in 02_Operational_Scenarios. If a narrative and an operational file differ, trust the operational file.

1. Read 00_ECOSYSTEM and TIMELINE for the shared calendar.
  2. Use Narrative Stories for onboarding, demos, and domain context.
  3. Use Operational Scenarios when writing seed data, tests, or checking state transitions.

Nothing in this folder introduces new entities, workflows, or system capabilities beyond what the operational layer already defines.

docs.title: Bento
docs.text: Bento is Ana Lourenço’s senior cat and the launch simulation’s clearest end-of-life animal narrative.

docs.title: Place in the household
docs.text: Bento shares Ana’s home with Pipoca, the cat adopted from shelter intake days earlier. While Pipoca represents new family growth, Bento carries the weight of older-animal care and closure inside the same May window.

docs.title: Care and outcome
docs.text:
João Marcelo’s clinical involvement for the Lourenço household includes Bento in the mid-May veterinary load described in the ecosystem cast. On 28 May 2026, Bento is recorded as deceased in the operational material. No additional invented ceremonies or diagnoses appear here — the fact is simply that the clinic’s records reflect death as a status change tied to real care history.

Pipoca’s 12 June scheduled visit remains on the calendar afterward, which is narratively important: the household continues with the surviving cat.

docs.title: Ecosystem role
docs.text: Bento exists so documentation can discuss bereavement and animal status in human terms, distinct from Pedro’s inactive client account or Quico’s indefinite internal waiting. Bento does not interact with external shelters or commercial returns.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
Ana is the owning client. Marcelo is the clinician context. Tiago’s shelter work applies to Pipoca, not Bento’s arc.

Operational detail: ANI_BENTO.md

docs.title: Felix
docs.text: Felix is Marta Ribeiro’s dog and the clinical anchor for a client who also generates commercial and scheduling friction.

docs.title: Care over time
docs.text:
Felix is adopted on 8 May from a local shelter mix, not from Patinhas. João Marcelo handles an acute limp across 13–14 May (in progress, then completed with delay). A follow-up on 17 May completes after Marta arrives late following traffic on the A3. A surgery-prep slot is cancelled on 24 May for a June date.

Felix does not adopt from shelter stock, does not die in the window, and does not transfer to external partners. His medical path stays comparatively straightforward compared to Jonas’s multi-specialty arc or Bento’s end of life.

docs.title: Ambient contact
docs.text: On 17 May, Felix’s appointment shares waiting-room chronology with Gonçalo Rego’s presence — two households in the same clinic moment without merging stories.

docs.title: Ecosystem role
docs.text: Felix lets readers connect Marta’s clinical normalcy to her commercial noise (return 18 May, cancellation 24 May, overdue invoice 5 June). The dog is the reason Marta keeps coming back medically even when retail and accounts receivable look uneven.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
Marta is the client. Marcelo is the veterinarian. Navarro is the commercial counterpart for purchases and returns tied to the same household week.

Operational detail: ANI_FELIX.md

docs.title: Jonas
docs.text: Jonas is Gonçalo Rego’s cat and the clinical plus retail driver for the busiest household in the launch window.

docs.title: Place in the household
docs.text: Unlike Rogerim, who arrives through Patinhas, Jonas is already Gonçalo’s animal when the May simulation begins. That makes Jonas the reference pet for repeat veterinary care and for shop behaviour tied to treatment — food and toys on 10 May, nutrition linked to dermatology on 18 May.

docs.title: Care over time
docs.text:
João Marcelo completes a general consultation on 12 May and dermatology on 16 May, the latter influencing diet decisions that Navarro’s desk reflects commercially two days later. A dermatology appointment remains scheduled for 10 June, with reminder activity on 9 June in the notification rhythm shared with other future visits.

Jonas does not pass through shelter internal status in the documented arc. Quico, Pipoca, and Rogerim own the intake side; Jonas owns ongoing client-animal medicine.

docs.title: Ecosystem role
docs.text:
Jonas validates multi-specialty scheduling, completed versus future visits, and the link between clinical outcomes and retail — without returns, death, or partner return events attached to his name.

Operational detail: ANI_JONAS.md

docs.title: Max
docs.text: Max is the return-to-partner animal in the launch window — movement back to Associação Patinhas do Ave under Tiago Mendes’s shelter management.

docs.title: Movement on 20 May
docs.text: On 20 May 2026, Tiago processes Max leaving client-facing placement and returning to Patinhas in the concession pattern described in the operational external-entity material. Max is not adopted by Gonçalo or Ana in the documented chronology; the narrative is closure of a partner relationship, not a new household.

docs.title: Contrast with other animals
docs.text: Rogerim and Pipoca travel into the clinic then out to families. Quico stays internal without partner return. Max travels back to the association, exercising the ecosystem’s need to show animals that do not only flow one direction.

docs.title: Ecosystem role
docs.text: Max supports partner shelter realism: associations both supply animals and receive them again when placement models require it. No commercial desk or Marta-style invoice story attaches to Max in the provided files.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
Tiago is the operational actor. Patinhas do Ave is the external counterpart. Active clients in the cast do not own Max in the May–June events captured here.

Operational detail: ANI_MAX.md

docs.title: Pipoca
docs.text: Pipoca is Ana Lourenço’s adopted cat, received through the same shelter corridor as Rogerim but on a parallel calendar.

docs.title: Origin and movement
docs.text: Tiago Mendes records Pipoca’s reception on 5 May, one day after Rogerim’s Patinhas intake. Pipoca stays internal until 9 May, when Ana completes adoption — the day after Gonçalo adopts Rogerim. The two adoptions back-to-back show the clinic handling multiple partner and internal placements in the same week.

docs.title: Life after adoption
docs.text:
Pipoca survives the household’s other major event: Bento’s death on 28 May. Pipoca’s forward path includes a scheduled visit on 12 June, placing the surviving cat still inside active care planning while Ana processes loss.

Pipoca does not appear in Marta’s retail friction, Pedro’s no-show, or Max’s return to Patinhas.

docs.title: Partners and people
docs.text:
Tiago owns intake and adoption. Ana is the client. João Marcelo is the clinician for the household; Bento carried the heavier mid-May clinical weight until deceased status. Pipoca represents continuity — adoption plus future wellness scheduling after bereavement.

Operational detail: ANI_PIPOCA.md

docs.title: Quico
docs.text: Quico is an abandonment intake who remains in internal shelter status through the end of the documented simulation — an animal still awaiting a home.

docs.title: How Quico arrives
docs.text: On 4 May 2026, Resgate Minhoto delivers Quico to the clinic loading bay — an abandonment case from a highway rest area, not an owner surrender. Tiago Mendes registers the animal and records the delivery; volunteers and clinic staff witness the handoff in the operational story. Quico widens the corridor beyond Patinhas-style shelter transfers while staying distinct from Gonçalo’s or Ana’s adoption paths.

docs.title: What does not happen in the window
docs.text: Quico does not complete adoption to Gonçalo, Ana, or Pedro within May–June 2026. Quico does not generate the clinical density of Jonas or Felix, or the return-and-invoice story of Marta. The operational point is waiting: internal animal, future placement still open.

docs.title: Ecosystem role
docs.text: Quico balances the success stories of Rogerim and Pipoca. Readers see a clinic that can hold animals in limbo as well as move them to families or back to partners (as with Max).

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
Tiago is the intake actor. Resgate Minhoto is the rescue partner. No owning client is attached in the launch cast.

Operational detail: ANI_QUICO.md

docs.title: Rogerim
docs.text: Rogerim is a shelter-to-adoption dog whose path defines the partner-intake story for Gonçalo Rego’s household.

docs.title: Origin and movement
docs.text:
On 4 May 2026, Tiago Mendes receives Rogerim from Associação Patinhas do Ave into the clinic’s internal shelter corridor. For four days Rogerim remains an internal animal awaiting a client link. On 8 May, Tiago completes the adoption that assigns Rogerim to Gonçalo Rego, who had registered two days earlier.

That short gap is narratively important: it mirrors realistic sequencing between partner transfer, client onboarding, and adoption completion without implying a failed placement.

docs.title: Life after adoption
docs.text: Once with Gonçalo, Rogerim is part of the anchor household narrative alongside Jonas the cat. The operational animal file centres on intake and adoption; Rogerim does not carry the multi-visit clinical density Jonas receives in May and June. Rogerim’s role in the ecosystem is successful partner shelter placement, not chronic specialty care.

docs.title: Partners and people
docs.text:
Patinhas do Ave is the external source. Tiago is the intake and adoption actor. Gonçalo is the owning client. João Marcelo and João Navarro serve the household indirectly through Jonas’s visits and purchases rather than through a long Rogerim-only clinical list in the provided material.

Operational detail: ANI_ROGERIM.md

docs.title: Ana Lourenço
docs.text: Ana Lourenço carries the adoption and loss thread for the launch simulation: one cat joins her household from shelter intake, another senior cat reaches the end of life during the same May window, and a future wellness visit remains on the calendar into June.

docs.title: Who she is in the ecosystem
docs.text:
Ana registered on 6 May 2026, the same day as Gonçalo Rego’s account and ahead of Marta Ribeiro’s desk registration on 8 May. She is an active client with Portuguese portal preferences and a household that mixes joyful intake with bereavement documentation.

Her animals in the operational cast are Pipoca, adopted after shelter reception, and Bento, described as a senior cat whose status moves to deceased within the simulation.

docs.title: How her story unfolds
docs.text:
On 5 May, Ana meets Pipoca through shelter photos while Pipoca arrives as an internal transfer from Patinhas. On 6 May, Isabel helps book Pipoca’s 12 June general check; Ivo and Isabel share the onboarding moment. Ana adopts Pipoca on 8 May — the same day as Gonçalo’s Rogerim adoption — with Tiago completing the adoption and Navarro selling a starter kit.

Bento’s arc is clinical and emotional rather than commercial. João Marcelo’s care for Bento leads to a clinical exit; on 28 May, Bento is recorded as deceased after decline (euthanasia in the operational narrative). Tiago also appears in recording that status change.

Pipoca’s 12 June general visit remains scheduled with Marcelo — booked when Ana became a client — placing Ana in the same “future appointment” family as Gonçalo’s Jonas dermatology date.

Ana does not appear in the return, overdue invoice, or authentication-typo clusters. Her narrative weight is continuity after loss: the clinic still serves the surviving cat and keeps a future visit on the books.

docs.title: Relationships that matter
docs.text:
Tiago Mendes connects Pipoca to shelter intake and adoption completion. João Marcelo is the clinician for both Bento’s final chapter and Pipoca’s ongoing care. João Navarro may appear at the margins of retail for other households but is not the centre of Ana’s documented friction. Isabel and Ivo sit in the usual desk and administrator roles for registration and coordination.

Ana’s story validates adoption from internal shelter stock, deceased animal status, and scheduled future care in one household — a different shape from Gonçalo’s two-pet busy calendar or Marta’s commercial disputes.

Operational detail: CLI_ANA_LOURENCO.md

docs.title: Gonçalo Rego
docs.text: Gonçalo Rego is the clinic’s most visible anchor client in the first launch weeks: he connects shelter intake, adoption, repeat shopping, and ongoing veterinary care for two household animals. He registered on 6 May 2026, after the shelter corridor had already begun to fill, and has remained an active portal user since.

docs.title: Who he is in the ecosystem
docs.text:
Gonçalo lives in the Braga area and uses the client portal with a Portuguese interface and dark theme preference. Ivo Sá created his account during the onboarding burst that followed the core team’s arrival. Before he had credentials, he had already met the front desk informally through Isabel Carvalho’s early presence at the clinic.

His animals are Rogerim, adopted from the Patinhas do Ave transfer on 8 May, and Jonas, a cat who was already under Gonçalo’s ownership before the May launch window. Together they make Gonçalo the reference household for “shelter animal becomes family member” and for repeat visits across more than one clinical specialty.

docs.title: How his story unfolds
docs.text:
Rogerim’s path begins on 4 May, when Tiago Mendes receives the dog from Associação Patinhas do Ave as an internal shelter animal. Gonçalo registers two days later; on 8 May Tiago completes the adoption that opens ownership for Rogerim. The interval between intake and adoption is deliberate in the simulation: it mirrors a short waiting period while the client account and visit planning catch up.

Jonas follows a steadier clinical rhythm with João Marcelo. A general consultation completes on 12 May; dermatology on 16 May leads to a diet change reflected in a shop purchase on 18 May, handled by João Navarro at the commercial desk. A further dermatology appointment remains scheduled for 10 June, with a reminder issued on 9 June as part of the clinic’s morning notification routine.

Retail visits on 10 May (food and toys) and 18 May (nutrition linked to Jonas’s care) show Gonçalo as a repeat buyer, not a one-time adopter. Marta Ribeiro crosses his path only in passing — they share the waiting room on 17 May when Marta arrives late for Felix’s visit — but the narrative does not tie them beyond that ambient contact.

docs.title: Friction and trust
docs.text: On 23 May, Gonçalo generates a cluster of failed sign-in attempts caused by repeated typos in his email address. The pattern is documented for audit and training purposes; occasional password mistakes appear as well. These episodes do not change his operational status as an active client; they illustrate how authentication history accumulates around a otherwise cooperative household.

docs.title: Relationships that matter
docs.text:
Tiago Mendes owns the shelter-facing steps for Rogerim. João Marcelo is Jonas’s clinician across general and dermatology work. João Navarro links consultations to invoices and products. Isabel bridges desk greeting and scheduling habits before and after her own return from absence. Ivo remains the administrator who registered the account and oversees platform configuration.

Gonçalo’s arc validates the clinic’s public face: adoption from a partner shelter, multi-animal ownership, appointment lifecycles including a future scheduled visit, commercial follow-through, and reminder-driven communication — without relying on edge cases such as returns or account inactivation.

Operational detail: CLI_GONCALO.md

docs.title: Marta Ribeiro
docs.text: Marta Ribeiro represents the commercial and scheduling stress side of the launch window: she buys, returns, arrives late, cancels, and leaves an invoice unpaid. She registered on 8 May 2026 at Isabel Carvalho’s desk with Ivo Sá creating the account, and remains active in the system through the simulation end. Her relationship with the clinic is more uneven than Gonçalo Rego’s steady household arc.

docs.title: Who she is in the ecosystem
docs.text:
Marta uses the client portal with Portuguese language settings and a light theme. Her primary animal is Felix, a young dog adopted on 8 May from a local shelter mix (not a Patinhas transfer). Clinical work runs through João Marcelo with an acute visit spanning 13–14 May and a follow-up on 17 May after she arrives late. Felix is the reason Marta appears in waiting-room and notification scenarios alongside other clients.

She is not a shelter adopter in the documented cast; her value to the simulation is retail friction, appointment discipline, and accounts receivable behaviour after the first month of operations.

docs.title: How her story unfolds
docs.text:
On 9 May, Marta completes a purchase at the desk with João Navarro — kibble and a lead — establishing her as a retail customer before the more difficult events. After Felix’s 13–14 May visit (which runs from in progress to completed with Marcelo delayed), Navarro invoices pharmacy items on 14 May; that invoice line later feeds the overdue story.

17 May is the turning point for scheduling reputation. Marta arrives late for Felix’s follow-up consultation after traffic on the A3. The visit still completes, but the lateness is recorded as part of the operational discipline layer. Gonçalo Rego is present in the same waiting-room moment, which ties two unrelated households in a single ambient chronology entry without merging their accounts.

18 May brings a return of a defective toy from an earlier purchase, processed again by João Navarro — a credit-note style commercial event distinct from the pharmacy pending invoice.

24 May, Marta cancels a surgery-prep appointment for a June slot. The cancellation is explicit in the timeline — it contrasts with Gonçalo’s forward-looking scheduled visit in June. Unlike Pedro Costa, Marta communicates; she is documented as not no-showing.

By 5 June, the pending invoice from 14 May is overdue. The clinic therefore carries both a progressing clinical path for Felix and an open receivable on the commercial side.

docs.title: Relationships that matter
docs.text:
João Navarro is her commercial counterpart for purchase and return. João Marcelo owns Felix’s clinical narrative. Isabel Carvalho and the broader desk team appear in scheduling and waiting-room context. Ivo Sá remains the administrator backdrop for account creation and platform configuration.

Marta’s story does not include adoption, shelter transfer, or account inactivation. It complements Gonçalo’s anchor household by showing how a single client can accumulate multiple operational signals — lateness, cancellation, return, overdue payment — while staying active.

Operational detail: CLI_MARTA_RIBEIRO.md

docs.title: Pedro Costa
docs.text: Pedro Costa is the discipline and inactivation client in the launch cast: a missed appointment, a dog who remains tied to the account, and a move to inactive status after the first month of operations.

docs.title: Who he is in the ecosystem
docs.text:
Pedro registered on 9 May 2026. His portal profile follows the same Portuguese, Braga-area pattern as other clients in the simulation. His animal Thor is named in the operational customer record even though Thor does not have a separate animal dossier in the Animals folder — the household is still understood as “client plus dog” for scheduling and no-show behaviour.

Pedro is not a shelter adopter in the documented timeline and does not drive retail returns or overdue invoices in the same way as Marta Ribeiro.

docs.title: How his story unfolds
docs.text:
On 15 May, Pedro does not attend a scheduled appointment. The no-show is a first-class operational event: it exists to exercise absence handling, client reputation signals, and follow-up posture without inventing a second missed visit or a complex clinical history.

After that sharp failure, Pedro cancels a second-chance appointment on 22 May (more than twenty-four hours ahead). Isabel notes the earlier no-call-no-show in internal commentary; Marcelo’s slot is freed without a no-show repeat.

On 2 June, Pedro’s client status becomes inactive — Ivo records a move abroad. Thor remains on the registry under the inactive client as a demo edge for reporting. Authentication attempts on an inactive account may still appear in the operational layer.

Pedro does not adopt from Patinhas, does not complete the multi-visit arcs of Gonçalo or Ana, and does not generate Gonçalo’s authentication typo cluster. His narrative is narrow: no-show, cancelled retry, then inactive client with animal still linked.

docs.title: Relationships that matter
docs.text:
Desk and clinical staff appear only as the generic clinic roles implied by the missed appointment — Marcelo’s calendar load includes other animals; Pedro’s no-show is not expanded into a rescheduled chain in the provided material. Tiago’s shelter work does not intersect Pedro’s household in the documented events.

Pedro exists so the ecosystem documentation can speak about failed attendance and inactive clients in human terms, alongside happier adoption stories and Marta’s commercial noise.

Operational detail: CLI_PEDRO_COSTA.md

docs.title: Bernardo Silva
docs.text: Bernardo Silva is the archived predecessor in the employee cast — a figure who explains continuity of roles without participating in the May–June 2026 launch events.

docs.title: Role in the ecosystem
docs.text:
Bernardo’s operational record places him in archived status from March 2026, before the simulation’s main window opens on 1 May. He does not receive shelter animals, complete adoptions, run the commercial desk, or appear on João Marcelo’s consultation calendar in the launch chronology.

His narrative function is organisational memory: new staff — Tiago, Navarro, Marcelo, Isabel — inherit a clinic that already had accounts, permissions, and possibly job titles shaped by earlier hires. Bernardo stands for “the person who used to hold the role” without requiring new workflows or events in May or June.

docs.title: What the story avoids
docs.text: Because no dated events attach to Bernardo inside the simulation window, this page does not invent farewell meetings, handover meetings, or disciplinary arcs. The only grounded facts are pre-launch archival and presence in the employee list for consistency with demo identity data.

docs.title: Relationships that matter
docs.text:
Ivo Sá as administrator is the implied counterpart for account lifecycle. Active employees do not depend on Bernardo for any timeline entry in the provided material; readers should treat him as historical context, not an active operator.

Operational detail: EMP_BERNARDO.md

docs.title: Isabel Carvalho
docs.text: Isabel Carvalho is the clinic’s hybrid figure: she coordinates the front desk after an early-May absence, and she is also a client with her own cats. That dual presence is deliberate in the launch simulation — the same person can greet Gonçalo and later sit in the waiting room logic as an animal owner.

docs.title: Role as employee
docs.text:
From 5–20 May, Isabel is in detected absence — not yet at the desk in the launch-week sense. Tiago and the absence layer document those gaps as staffing signals. On 6 May she still helps Ana Lourenço by phone to request Pipoca’s June booking before Ana’s adoption completes. From 21 May onward she is the active front desk; Gonçalo’s informal early contact fits that bridge period.

She does not own shelter transfers, supplier orders, or administrator configuration — Ivo, Tiago, and Navarro hold those edges.

docs.title: Role as client
docs.text:
As a client, Isabel keeps Tico, Teco, and Jerónimo in the household cast. 22 May is Tico’s chain: scheduling through clinical completion and invoicing with João Marcelo. A 21 May morning reminder targets Tico as a client notification. Teco and Jerónimo are named cohabiting cats without separate dated visit arcs in the provided material.

A 3 June pending absence appears on the employee side after the main launch window — another staffing beat without inventing new clinical events.

Isabel’s client animals are not duplicated as standalone files in the Animals operational folder; only Tico’s dated clinical event is spelled out in depth. Narratives for Teco and Jerónimo therefore remain implicit inside Isabel’s story rather than as invented adventures.

docs.title: Why she matters to the ecosystem
docs.text: Isabel proves that employee and client boundaries can coexist in one real organisation: desk coordination, public support scenarios, and “my cat’s appointment” can reference the same person without merging accounts incorrectly in the reader’s mind — the operational layer keeps the rules; this layer keeps the human picture.

docs.title: Relationships that matter
docs.text:
João Marcelo is Tico’s clinician on 22 May. Gonçalo is an early informal contact. Tiago appears in absence detection context. Other clients — Marta, Ana, Pedro — do not centre on Isabel in the documented events.

Operational detail: EMP_CLI_ISABEL.md

docs.title: Ivo Sá
docs.text: Ivo Sá is the platform administrator for MiaCaoMigo Braga in the launch simulation. He is present from the first day of the operational window and owns the configuration and account-creation work that lets the rest of the cast appear on the timeline.

docs.title: Role in the ecosystem
docs.text:
As administrator, Ivo sits above the day-to-day shelter, clinical, and commercial flows. He is not the narrative centre of adoption or consultation stories, but he is the person who makes those stories possible in the system: client registrations for Gonçalo, Marta, Ana, and Pedro fall within the onboarding burst he supports, and employee accounts for Tiago, Navarro, Marcelo, and Isabel depend on the same administrative layer.

His work aligns with 1 May 2026 as the simulation anchor — clinic go-live, team presence, and the start of chronology entries that reference administrator actions.

docs.title: How he interacts with others
docs.text:
Tiago Mendes depends on administrative stability to record shelter intakes and adoptions. João Navarro and João Marcelo need roles, schedules, and permissions consistent with commercial desk and veterinary lead duties. Isabel Carvalho’s hybrid identity — employee and client — also passes through the administrative boundary Ivo represents.

When Gonçalo Rego later generates failed sign-in attempts, the audit flavour of those events is administrator-relevant even though Ivo is not portrayed as personally resetting passwords in the narrative material.

docs.title: What his story is not
docs.text:
The operational layer does not assign Ivo a heavy clinical calendar, shelter transfers, or retail returns. His narrative is enabling infrastructure: the clinic’s digital twin stays coherent while front-of-house stories play out.

Operational detail: EMP_IVO.md

docs.title: João Marcelo
docs.text: João Marcelo is the veterinary lead for the Braga launch window. Consultations, follow-ups, specialty visits, end-of-life recording, and scheduling pressure on his calendar define his place in the ecosystem.

docs.title: Role in the ecosystem
docs.text:
Marcelo completes or owns the clinical threads for Felix (Marta Ribeiro’s dog), Jonas (Gonçalo Rego’s cat across general and dermatology), Bento (Ana Lourenço’s senior cat through to deceased status on 28 May), and Tico (Isabel Carvalho’s cat as client animal on 22 May with prescription follow-through in the operational chain). He is the named clinician when the timeline needs completed visits, late arrival still completed, or future scheduled visits tied to medical specialties.

11 May is his stress day in the chronology: a double-booking event exercises calendar conflict handling without inventing a second veterinarian. The narrative treats that day as operational load, not personal drama.

docs.title: Clinical rhythm
docs.text:
Felix’s path — 10 May consultation and 17 May follow-up after Marta arrives late — anchors the “busy dog owner” clinical side. Jonas’s 12 May general and 16 May dermatology visits link directly to Gonçalo’s retail follow-up. Bento’s decline gives the ecosystem a deceased animal signal tied to real care rather than admin deletion. Tico’s 22 May visit connects the hybrid Isabel storyline back to Marcelo as vet, not only as desk coordinator.

Marcelo does not process shelter intakes, Patinhas transfers, or NorteVet purchase orders. Tiago and Navarro own those planes.

docs.title: Relationships that matter
docs.text:
Gonçalo, Marta, Ana, and Isabel-as-client are his household-facing clients in the cast. Pedro Costa’s no-show implies a scheduled Marcelo slot but the operational animal files centre on Thor only through Pedro’s customer record. Isabel as employee re-enters after absence detection; Marcelo’s calendar is independent of her desk return except where shared days collide.

Marcelo’s narrative is the medical credibility of the clinic during the first six weeks — including one deliberate scheduling failure mode on 11 May.

Operational detail: EMP_J_MARCELO.md

docs.title: João Navarro
docs.text: João Navarro is the commercial desk lead in the launch simulation. Purchases, returns, supplier-facing purchase orders, and the invoice side of client relationships run through his timeline more than through any other employee.

docs.title: Role in the ecosystem
docs.text:
Navarro registers commercially significant moments for Marta Ribeiro — a purchase on 10 May and a return on 18 May — and supports Gonçalo Rego when retail aligns with Jonas’s nutrition change after dermatology. He is the natural counterpart when the ecosystem needs stock movement tied to clients rather than shelter intake.

On 19 May, his work extends to NorteVet Supply Lda with a purchase order event, linking the clinic’s back office to an external supplier without turning the narrative into inventory schema language.

docs.title: How he differs from clinical staff
docs.text:
João Marcelo owns consultation completion, lateness, cancellations, and clinical load including the 11 May double-booking stress day. Navarro stays on the money and goods plane: what was sold, what came back, what was ordered from a wholesaler, and which invoice is overdue for Marta by 5 June.

He does not adopt animals or receive shelter transfers. Tiago Mendes hands off to Navarro once animals belong to clients who shop.

docs.title: Relationships that matter
docs.text:
Marta is his friction client; Gonçalo is his repeat buyer; Marta’s overdue invoice closes the commercial arc into June. NorteVet is the supplier partner named in his chronology. Ivo Sá remains the administrator backdrop.

Navarro’s story makes the clinic feel like a business as well as a care site — returns and payables sit alongside Felix’s visits in the same calendar.

Operational detail: EMP_J_NAVARRO.md

docs.title: Tiago Mendes
docs.text: Tiago Mendes is the clinic’s animal and shelter manager in the launch window. His work connects external partner intake, internal shelter animals, adoptions, and one concession back to a partner organisation.

docs.title: Role in the ecosystem
docs.text:
From 4 May onward, Tiago is the operational face of “animal arrives from outside” and “animal leaves for adoption or return.” He receives Rogerim from Associação Patinhas do Ave and later completes Gonçalo Rego’s adoption. He receives Pipoca before Ana Lourenço’s adoption. He handles Quico as an abandonment intake who remains internally awaiting a home. On 20 May, he processes Max moving back to Patinhas under a concession pattern documented in the external partner story.

Tiago also appears in absence detection entries tied to Isabel Carvalho’s early May gap — the chronology records detected absences before Isabel returns to desk coordination. That linkage is operational, not a personal conflict narrative; it shows how staffing visibility intersects shelter work.

docs.title: Rhythm of the first weeks
docs.text:
The first week clusters partner transfers and internal status: Rogerim and Pipoca establish the shelter corridor; Quico adds a non-partner abandonment path; Max closes the loop with Patinhas on return. Adoptions to Gonçalo and Ana land on 8 and 9 May, giving Tiago back-to-back “animal becomes family member” completions.

Tiago does not own Felix’s clinical arc, Marta’s returns, or Pedro’s no-show. His story stays on the animal lifecycle side of the house.

docs.title: Relationships that matter
docs.text:
Associação Patinhas do Ave is his most frequent external counterpart. Gonçalo and Ana are the adopting clients for Rogerim and Pipoca. João Marcelo and João Navarro take over after animals attach to clients or when clinical and commercial events supersede intake.

Tiago’s narrative is the bridge between external entities and household animals inside Braga operations.

Operational detail: EMP_TIAGO.md

docs.title: NorteVet Supply Lda
docs.text: NorteVet Supply Lda is the clinic’s wholesale supplier in the launch simulation — the commercial back office counterpart to Marta Ribeiro’s retail purchases at the front desk.

docs.title: Role in the network
docs.text:
On 19 May 2026, João Navarro’s timeline includes a purchase order event with NorteVet. That single dated anchor ties the ecosystem to inbound stock from outside without describing product catalogs or inventory tables in this layer.

NorteVet does not adopt animals, receive shelter returns, or appear in client waiting rooms. It exists so the clinic is modeled as both care site and stocked business.

docs.title: Distinction from welfare partners
docs.text: Associação Patinhas do Ave and Resgate Minhoto belong to animal welfare flows. NorteVet belongs to supply chain flows. Keeping that separation clear helps readers understand why Navarro, not Tiago, owns the relationship in the chronology.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
Navarro is the named employee contact. Ivo as administrator underpins vendor master data in the operational world. Clients such as Gonçalo and Marta feel NorteVet only indirectly when desk sales depend on stocked goods — the narrative does not claim a specific product line for the 19 May order beyond what operational files state.

Operational detail: EXT_NORTEVET_SUPPLY.md

docs.title: Associação Patinhas do Ave
docs.text: Associação Patinhas do Ave is a partner shelter in the Braga launch ecosystem. Animals move between the association and MiaCaoMigo’s internal shelter corridor under Tiago Mendes’s management.

docs.title: Role in the network
docs.text:
Patinhas is the external organisation behind Rogerim’s intake on 4 May and Gonçalo Rego’s adoption on 8 May. The same partner thread includes Max returning on 20 May — a concession-style movement that shows the association is not only a one-way supplier of dogs.

The operational material positions Patinhas as the named shelter partner for transfer in and return out, distinct from Resgate Minhoto’s rescue identity and from NorteVet’s commercial supply role.

docs.title: Interaction rhythm
docs.text:
Early May concentrates incoming partner animals that become internal shelter stock and then client adoptions. Mid-May adds outgoing movement for Max, balancing Rogerim’s successful placement narrative.

Patinhas does not appear as Marta’s retail supplier or as the source for Quico’s abandonment intake in the documented events.

docs.title: People on the clinic side
docs.text:
Tiago Mendes is the consistent operational face. Gonçalo is the adopting client for Rogerim. Ivo and desk staff sit in the background as administrators and coordinators; João Marcelo’s work begins after animals attach to clients.

Patinhas makes the clinic legible as embedded in a local welfare network, not as an isolated practice.

Operational detail: EXT_PATINHAS_AVE.md

docs.title: Resgate Minhoto
docs.text: Resgate Minhoto is the launch simulation’s emergency rescue partner — distinct from Associação Patinhas do Ave’s shelter transfers and from NorteVet’s wholesale supply role.

docs.title: Role in the network
docs.text:
Based in the Guimarães periphery, Resgate Minhoto handles short-notice intakes when animals are found in distress rather than handed over through a standing shelter pipeline. Volunteers coordinate with the clinic at the loading bay; delivery witnesses in the operational material often include Tiago Mendes and sometimes João Marcelo in an off-clinical assist role.

The dated anchor for this partner is 4 May 2026, when Resgate Minhoto delivers Quico — a dog abandoned near a highway rest area. Tiago registers Quico and records the delivery; Quico remains internal, in kennel B-12 in the operational notes, awaiting adoption through the end of the May–June window.

docs.title: Distinction from Patinhas
docs.text: Patinhas supplies Rogerim and Pipoca through transfer deliveries that precede client adoptions. Resgate Minhoto supplies rescue urgency and abandonment origin language without placing Quico into Gonçalo’s or Ana’s households in the documented chronology.

docs.title: Clinic relationships
docs.text:
Tiago is the consistent handler for intake. Marcelo appears at the margins of delivery witness lists. No retail or invoice arc runs through Resgate Minhoto — Navarro and client purchases sit on a different plane.

Resgate Minhoto makes the external cast three-shaped: shelter partner, rescue partner, supplier.

Operational detail: EXT_RESCATE_MINHO.md

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Operational Scenarios document:

  • who did what and when in machine-checkable terms;
  • workflow states (appointments, animals, invoices, absences, clients);
  • references to services and procedures (sp_*, fn_*) where validation requires them;
  • cross-links between cast members and OPS guides.

They are the consistency contract between this portal and 01_MiaCaoMigo_DataLayer seed/QA material. They are not a substitute for SQL documentation in 04_Architecture.

docs.title: Operations — Appointment States
docs.text:
Timeline: TIMELINE_LAUNCH_2026.md · Ecosystem: 00_ECOSYSTEM.md

Platform enum appointment_status: scheduled, in_progress, completed, cancelled, no_show, late.

There is no requested row state — front-desk “requests” are human intake before sp_create_appointment.

docs.title: 1. Requested (operational, pre-system)
docs.text:
Context What happens Isabel → Marcelo Isabel captures paper form; verifies ownership; calls sp_create_appointment with Marcelo as id_emp Ana → Pipoca 6 May: Ana asks for post-adoption check; Isabel books once id_cli exists Gonçalo portal Client UI gathers slot preference; backend still ends in scheduled

Related: EMP_CLI_ISABEL, CLI_ANA

docs.title: 2. Scheduled (sp_create_appointment)
docs.text:
Case Animal Client Vet When Future dermatology Jonas Gonçalo Marcelo 10 Jun 2026 Post-adoption check Pipoca Ana Marcelo 12 Jun 2026 Cancelled later Kika proxy → Marta's Felix Marta Marcelo 24 May cancel of different June surgery slot

Rules enforced on insert:

  • fn_validate_animal_client_relationship
  • fn_validate_appointment_vet_specialty (expert)
  • fn_block_appointment_if_vet_unavailable
  • ex_appointment_vet_overlap (30 min GiST, scheduled only)
  • fn_block_past_appointments

Notification: row appears in vw_scheduled_appointments_tomorrow → cron at 08:00 day before.

docs.title: 3. Late (read model, still scheduled in DB)
docs.text:
Case Story Marta / Felix 17 May: sch_dat_app passed while owner stuck in traffic; portal lists late via fn_list_client_appointments case expression; Marcelo starts visit anyway → in_progress

DB remains scheduled until sp_start_appointment; UI may show late when sch_dat_app < now().

docs.title: 4. In progress (sp_start_appointment)
docs.text:
Case Story Felix / Marta 13 May: Marcelo delayed (prior visit overran); sta_dat_app set; Isabel reassures waiting room Stress day 11 May: two overlapping risks taught team to stagger slots

Only from scheduled (or effectively scheduled + late arrival).

docs.title: 5. Completed (sp_end_appointment)
docs.text:
Case id_spe Billing Jonas routine geral id_inv optional Jonas dermatology dermatology Navarro lines 18 May Tico geral id_inv + rel_pre_prod ×2 Felix geral paid invoice Ana / Pipoca geral pending → paid

Follow-ups: sp_prescription_for_appointment, overall_assessment, anamnesis.

docs.title: 6. Cancelled (sp_cancel_appointment)
docs.text:
Case Cause Rule Marta surgery prep Family travel; rebooks August verbally Cancelled 24 May for slot >24h out Historical Bernardo-era row in archive Terminal — no edits

Fails if inside 24h window — Isabel must coordinate Marcelo override via reschedule narrative (not in schema).

docs.title: 7. No show (sp_auto_update_no_show_appointments)
docs.text:
Case Story Pedro / dog Thor 15 May 11:00: owner never arrived; cron 00:05 next day sets no_show; reminder was ignored

Prior state: scheduled. Vet absence would have blocked booking via fn_block_appointment_if_vet_unavailable.

docs.text:
[requested] ──sp_create_appointment──► scheduled
scheduled ──sp_start_appointment──► in_progress
